subject: Next steps: ToolGrid POC architecture + SDK/Auth checklist
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@toolgrid.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: ToolGrid POC architecture + SDK/Auth checklist

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the POC scope and get your infra team unblocked. High-level notes from today:

- Goal: 3-week POC to validate (a) inference latency for 512-token responses under concurrent user load (~120 RPS peak), (b) embeddings-based search + lightweight reranking for Knowledge Base, and (c) tool/function calling to 3 downstream systems (search, billing, HR API).
- Primary success metrics: 95th percentile gen latency < 220ms for cached prefixes, retrieval latency (embedding vector nearest neighbor) < 40ms, reranker accuracy lift >= 12% over current lexical baseline.

Recommended POC architecture (short):
1) SDK & runtime: use Redwood JS SDK (server-side Node) for initial POC. Enable streaming for UI latency and prefix caching on the client.
2) Auth: start with API key for speed of setup; migrate to OIDC (Dex/Okta) for production SSO. We can issue scoped API keys per environment.
3) Routing & routing policies: route read-heavy inference to hosted nodes in us-west for latency; fallback to cheaper quantized model variant in us-east for cost/backfill. Add a shutdown fallback policy for heavy spikes.
4) Embeddings + rerankers: store dense vectors in your existing Milvus cluster. We'll ship embedding hooks; recommend async refresh and hybrid rerank (lexical filter -> embedding recall -> lightweight transformer reranker).
5) Tool/function calling model: define explicit tool schema for each action. Minimal set we proposed:
   - search_documents(query: string, top_k: int) -> list[result_id]
   - create_billing_ticket(payload: object) -> {ticket_id, status}
   - hr_lookup(employee_id: string) -> {name, email, manager}

Tool calling patterns & error handling notes:
- Parallel calls: fan-out to non-dependent tools (e.g., search and analytics) in parallel; aggregate results with timeouts (~200ms default).
- Deterministic vs non-deterministic tools: treat external side-effecting calls (billing) as single-call, confirm via two-phase commit from app layer if needed.
- Failure modes: soft-fail (return best-effort response with telemetry) vs hard-fail (block response). For POC, default to soft-fail + error banner in UI.

Attachments: draft SOW attached (toolgrid-poc-sow-v1.pdf) and small SDK/auth matrix.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We (Redwood) will deliver a 1-page technical plan + config snippets for SDK, auth, routing by EOD tomorrow.
2) ToolGrid to confirm target peak RPS and example KB size (~GBs of docs).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive this week (we suggested Wed noon PT).

Can you confirm the RPS and whether your Milvus cluster is accessible from our staging VPC (or whether you prefer us to host an embedding index during the POC)?

Cheers,

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: 2028-06-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: ToolGrid POC architecture + SDK/Auth checklist

Vanessa — thanks, this is a great summary. A few clarifying Qs from our infra lead:

- RPS: we expect 100–140 RPS peak during our busiest workflows; steady-state ~30 RPS.
- KB size: roughly 60 GB of documents (already chunked). Latency target for retrieval end-to-end is aggressive, so caching/retrieval tiering will be important.
- Milvus: yes, hosted in our cloud account but currently not open to external VPCs. We can open a read-only endpoint for your staging cluster or provide a sample export of vectors. Which do you recommend for the cleanest evaluation?

Also, curious about the reranker model: are you proposing running the reranker on Redwood-hosted inference or locally in our VPC? Latency and cost assumptions differ.

Happy to do Wed 11:30am PT (works for us) — please send calendar invite.

Subject: Re: Next steps: ToolGrid POC architecture + SDK/Auth checklist

Looping in a couple of quick commercial/ops notes so everyone has context: 

- Given the 100–140 RPS peak and the 95th latency target, this POC will be most realistic on a Dedicated pool or a high-memory hosted configuration with aggressive batching disabled for cold prefixes. If ToolGrid needs strict SLOs for demos, we should include a Dedicated sizing option in the SOW.
- Pricing note: POC quote will assume a short-term burst configuration; if you move to Dedicated there is a monthly commit. We can provide an illustrative cost delta in the plan deliverable tomorrow.
- Legal/procurement: ToolGrid indicated procurement window is 3–4 weeks. We should prioritize getting the SOW and an initial security questionnaire answered to avoid delays.

A couple of technical flags for Vanessa's plan: 
- If Milvus can't be opened to our staging VPC, recommend a read-only vector snapshot loaded into a Redwood-managed index for POC (we'll handle vector ingestion and ensure the sample size mimics your production distribution).
- For tool calling, add request tracing headers and token exchange logs to ensure we can map user requests to side effects for debugging.

I'll be on the deep-dive Wed 11:30am PT. Sending a calendar hold now.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: ToolGrid POC architecture + SDK/Auth checklist

Alex — thanks for the fast reply and confirming RPS/Kb size. Quick decisions we made in-thread so the engineering teams can move forward: 

Decisions for POC:
- Milvus access: ToolGrid to provide a read-only vector snapshot (preferred). If that takes longer than 48 hours, Redwood will stand up a sample managed index and ingest a representative subset you provide.
- Reranker placement: run reranker on Redwood-hosted inference in the POC to simplify instrumentation; we will provide latency profiles and cost estimates.
- Auth: start with scoped API keys; we'll include an OIDC migration plan in the SOW for production.
- Tool calling: define explicit tool schemas. For billing operations, Redwood will surface the create_billing_ticket response but not attempt automatic retries for side-effecting calls — app layer to handle compensating actions.

Deliverables + owners: 
1) Redwood: 1-page technical plan + SDK snippets (Vanessa) — EOD tomorrow.
2) Redwood: SOW + Dedicated sizing option (Sean) — EOD Friday.
3) ToolGrid: read-only vector snapshot or sample export + confirmation of any blocking network policies (Alex) — 48 hours.
4) Joint: 60-min deep-dive Wed 11:30am PT — calendar invite sent (holding).

I'll attach the SDK auth matrix and a short config example for the tool schemas after this note. If anything above looks off, flag it here and we'll correct before the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
